task: Define and visually curate the Autonomous Product Foundry system, page architecture, and proof-gated customer journey.
surface: Architecture documentation and future FrankX Foundry, portal, Academy, and community experience specification.
audience: Frank, selected collaborators, product builders, independent verifiers, and future Foundry customers.
first_read: Turn one workflow into a verified agent-delivered product without buying Frank's implementation hours.

references.label: FrankX brand design system
references.reason: Provides the restrained dual-spectrum obsidian system and technical editorial posture.

references.label: Premium asset standard
references.reason: Requires the correct asset tier and blocks abstract filler or fake UI as proof.

references.label: Autonomous Foundry control plane
references.reason: Supplies the exact system relationships represented by the diagrams.

keep: Clear live, prototype, design-only, and human-gated status
FrankX editorial restraint and proof-first hierarchy
A prose or table equivalent next to every diagram
avoid: AI orbs, node clouds, generic 3D primitives, and decorative system maps
Fake dashboards, fabricated metrics, and unlabeled fixtures
Garish gradients, crowded card grids, and sales-pressure patterns
Public UI claims before actual preview inspection
direction.signature: The Outcome Receipt evolves from workflow to product, entitlement, agent run, verification, credits, release, and rollback.
system: Obsidian background and restrained emerald/cyan technical signals
Amber only for human value and approval boundaries
Outfit or Poppins display, Inter body, JetBrains Mono receipts
Tier C exact vector diagrams now; Tier A redacted real receipts when product runs exist
Motion expresses causality and state only, with a complete reduced-motion route

asset_quality.why_premium: Exact system-authored diagrams and an ownable Outcome Receipt are the correct medium for a control-plane specification; generated decoration would reduce trust.

artifacts.notes: Text and Mermaid source inspected; diagrams have adjacent prose/table equivalents.
Control-plane and entitlement state relationships inspected in source form.
Page, state, asset, accessibility, and motion contracts inspected; no rendered page exists yet.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C exact vector/system diagrams are the correct medium for architecture documentation.

checks.name: export-inspection
checks.evidence: No public UI or rendered diagram export was produced because PP admission is HOLD; source inspection is not substituted for browser inspection.

checks.name: visual-qa
checks.evidence: Desktop/mobile/reduced-motion QA begins only when an authorized preview implementation exists.

checks.name: exact-information
checks.evidence: Every visual relationship is sourced from the machine-readable control-plane contract and accompanied by text.

score.notes: Strongest: the Outcome Receipt gives the system an ownable proof language. Weakest: no rendered implementation or responsive inspection exists. Change after critique: all abstract hero concepts were removed in favor of exact diagrams and future real receipts. Decision: iterate before any public ship.

known_risks: Mermaid rendering can vary by host and must be inspected where the docs are published.
A future UI could drift into generic dashboards unless the Outcome Receipt remains the primary proof object.
The experience cannot score as shippable until real product receipts and a Vercel preview are inspected.
